name: Alnair
description: A subgiant of type B7 IV 31.0 parsecs away, 3.4 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Narrabri intensity interferometer.

paper.credit: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417

radius.source: Computed here, not printed by a paper: 3.4 +/- 0.23 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.02 +/- 0.07 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 32.29 +/- 0.21 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP)

temperature.source: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 209952: effective temperature 14050 +/- 540 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared

distance.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 109268: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 32.29 +/- 0.21 mas, inverted

text.card: A subgiant of type B7 IV, 31 parsecs away: 3.4 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.02 milliarcseconds, which at its distance is 3.4 solar radii, and its surface is at 14,050 K.
text.locator: Tables 1 and 6, HD 209952: MK type, limb-darkened diameter, effective temperature

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6560604777055249536 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
